articles.title: Brickbat: XX Marks the Spot
articles.content:
A federal appeals court ruled in favor of four Bow, New Hampshire, parents who said their First Amendment rights were violated after they wore pink "XX" wristbands at a girls' soccer game to protest transgender athletes competing in girls' sports. School officials accused the parents of harassing, intimidating, and threatening a player on the other team. Two of the parents also received no-trespass orders banning them from school property. When the parents refused to remove the wristbands, the school stopped the game and had police escort them away. The parents sued, arguing they were peacefully expressing their views. A lower court initially sided with the school district, but the First Circuit Court of Appeals overturned that decision and send it back to a lower court. The appeals court ruled that the parents' silent display of the wristbands did not amount to harassment or disruption and that the school had improperly punished them for the viewpoint they expressed.

The post Brickbat: XX Marks the Spot appeared first on Reason Magazine.

articles.title: Open Thread
articles.content:
**尤金·沃洛赫：密苏里藐视法院判决**
**尤金·沃洛赫**是斯坦福胡佛研究所的托马斯·M·西贝尔高级研究员，加州大学洛杉矶分校（UCLA）法学院加里·T·施瓦茨杰出法学教授，现为荣休教授。正如其他博主的观点一样，他的文章观点仅代表个人，不代表任何机构立场。他同时也是《言论自由无噪音》播客的联合主持人。

密苏里州一名法官日前对一起案件做出了藐视法院的判决。此案涉及一名拒绝执行法院命令的当事人，法官认为其行为构成对法院的藐视。该判决引发了法律界的广泛关注，美国宪法第一修正案专家尤金·沃洛赫教授发表了深入评论。

沃洛赫教授指出，藐视法院判决虽然在法律程序中较为常见，但此次判决的特殊性在于涉及言论自由的争议。当事人拒绝执行的命令涉及言论内容，而非简单的行为要求。这引发了关于言论自由与法院权威的平衡问题。

密苏里州的法律界人士表示，该判决可能对本州的司法实践产生重要影响。此前类似案件中，法院通常会优先考虑言论自由的保护，而非直接判定藐视。此次判决的严厉性表明法院对言论行为的容忍度可能在降低。

沃洛赫教授强调，尽管藐视法院判决在理论上是合法的，但需要审慎评估其对言论自由的潜在影响。他建议法律界应就此次判决进行深入讨论，以明确言论自由与法院权威的边界。

密苏里州法院的判决文书显示，当事人被指控拒绝履行法院命令，并公开发表挑衅性言论。法官认为其行为不但违反了法院命令，还挑战了司法权威。因此，法院决定对其处以罚款并要求其道歉。

此案的争议焦点在于，当事人是否可以以言论自由为由拒绝执行法院命令。沃洛赫教授认为，言论自由并非绝对，尤其是在涉及司法程序的情况下。然而，法院在判决时应充分考虑言论内容的合理性和公共利益。

密苏里州的法律界人士表示，此次判决可能会对类似案件产生示范效应。未来，法院在处理言论自由与藐视法院的冲突时，可能会更加倾向于维护司法权威。

沃洛赫教授还指出，此次判决引发的讨论不仅限于密苏里州，其他州的法律界也应关注这一案件的发展。言论自由与司法权威的平衡问题需要更广泛的讨论，以确保法律的公正性和可行性。

**关键词：言论自由、藐视法院、密苏里州、尤金·沃洛赫、司法权威**

articles.title: The Contempt Judgment From Missouri
articles.content:
密苏里州的混乱局势仍在继续。就在美国最高法院暂停克拉克法官裁决的同一时间，密苏里州最高法院召开紧急听证会，讨论是否应当对州务卿丹尼·霍斯金斯(Denny Hoskins)以藐视法庭罪处罚。此时，由于最高法院已暂停克拉克法官的裁决，霍斯金斯不再面临两项冲突的禁令，并同意执行2022年划分的选区地图。最终，法院裁定霍斯金斯已"消除了"藐视法庭罪的责任，因此未予以任何惩罚。

然而，在大约16小时内，州务卿同时受到两项禁令的约束。密苏里州最高法院要求他使用2022年的选区地图，而美国东部密苏里联邦地区法院则命令他使用2026年的选区地图。哪一家法院的命令更优先？答案是：两家法院均无优先权。它们都是具有管辖权的法院，均发布了具有约束力的命令。一家法院并不高于另一家。实际上，密苏里州最高法院和第八巡回上诉法院的冲突裁决也会导致同样的问题。如果霍斯金斯必须选择遵守哪一项判决，他不得不在两者之间做出选择。但这种选择本身就有代价。如果他遵守州法院的裁决，克拉克法官可能会对他提出藐视法庭罪；如果他遵守联邦法院的裁决，密苏里州最高法院也可能以藐视法庭罪追究他。

在这些非常罕见的情况下，最高法院在48小时内拒绝推翻州法院的裁决，并暂停了联邦法院的裁决，因此霍斯金斯从最高层得到了明确的指引。但在正常情况下，这种冲突的禁令可能会持续数天、数周，甚至更长时间。

这种情况也曾在阿拉巴马州的同性婚姻诉讼中出现过。州内的遗嘱法官在发放结婚证时，同时受到来自联邦法官和阿拉巴马州最高法院的冲突命令约束。最终，奥伯格费尔案(Obergefell)解决了这一问题，但在此之前，遗嘱法官必须选择哪家法院可能会以藐视法庭罪对他们进行威胁。

霍华德·瓦瑟曼(Howard Wasserman)和我在2016年的一篇文章中解释了这一动态：
在奥伯格费尔案判决后的最初几天里，一些遗嘱法官试图回避为同性伴侣发放结婚证，或完全拒绝发放结婚证。但现已生效的集体禁令迅速结束了这些尝试，确保了无需进一步步骤即可实现合规。如果遗嘱法官拒绝发放结婚证，一方不需要提起新的诉讼或获得新的禁令。他们可以直接向联邦法官格兰纳德(Judge Granade)申请执行现有禁令的命令，而无需进一步的宪法分析。法院将迅速命令遗嘱法官根据禁令的条款发放结婚证，如果不遵守将被处以民事藐视。

密苏里州最高法院可能应该等待美国最高法院作出裁决后，再设定藐视法庭程序的口头辩论。我希望在“Show-Me州”能够保持理性。目前局势过于紧张。
articles.summary:
The wild ride in Missouri continues. Around the same time that the United States Supreme Court stayed Judge Clark's ruling, the Missouri Supreme Court held an emergency hearing about whether Secretary of State Denny Hoskins should be held in contempt. By that time, because Judge Clark's ruling was stayed by the Supreme Court, Hoskins was no longer subject to dueling injunctions, and thus agreed to enforce the 2022 maps. Ultimately, the court ruled that Hoskins "purged himself" of contempt, and therefore imposed no punishment.

Yet, for a period of about 16 hours, the Secretary of State was subject to two sets of injunctions. The Missouri Supreme Court ordered him to use the 2022 maps. And the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Missouri ordered him to use the 2026 maps. Which of these two courts prevails? Neither. They are both courts of competent jurisdiction that issued binding orders. One is not higher than the other. Indeed, conflicting rulings from the Missouri Supreme Court and the Eighth Circuit would present the same issue.  Hoskins, if push came to shove, would have to choose which judgment he wishes to comply with. But that choice entails costs. If he complied with the state court ruling, Judge Clark could have held him in contempt. If he complied with the federal court ruling, the Missouri Supreme Court could have held him contempt.

Under these very unusual circumstances, the Supreme Court in the span of 48 hours declined to disturb the state court ruling and stayed the federal court ruling, so Hoskins got some definitive guidance from up to. But in the normal course, these sorts of dueling injunctions would co-exist for days, weeks, or even longer.

This sort of dynamic played out in Alabama during the same-sex marriage litigation. State probate judges who issued our marriage licenses were subject to conflicting orders from a federal judge in Mobile and the Alabama Supreme Court. Ultimately, Obergefell settled the matter, but in the interim, the state probate judges had to pick which court might threaten them with contempt.

Howard Wasserman and I explained the dynamics in our 2016 article:

While the days immediately following Obergefell were marked by scattered attempts by some probate judges to avoid issuing licenses to same-sex couples or to avoid issuing licenses at all, the now effective class injunction quickly ended those efforts by ensuring compliance without need for that additional step. A couple denied a license by a probate judge would not have to initiate a new lawsuit or obtain a new injunction. They instead could go directly to [Federal] Judge Granade for an order enforcing the existing injunction, with no further constitutional analysis required. The court would promptly order the probate judge to issue licenses under the terms of the injunction, with failure to comply sanctioned by civil contempt.

The Missouri Supreme Court probably should have waited until the Supreme Court ruled before it set oral argument for contempt proceedings. I hope cooler heads prevail in the Show-Me state. Things are a bit too hot right now.

The post The Contempt Judgment From Missouri appeared first on Reason Magazine.

articles.title: Marijuana Contracts Are Not Enforceable in Federal Court
articles.content:
目前美国有两打州在州际法下合法化大麻的成年人持有行为。更多州则允许医用大麻的持有和使用。然而，联邦法律下大麻分销和持有依然非法。尽管联邦政府可能不会投入大量资源来执行联邦大麻禁令，但大麻在联邦法律中的非法性仍可能产生重要后果（虽然对于枪支拥有者来说，由于最高法院在《合众国诉赫曼尼》案的判决，这些后果相对较少）。

今天美国联邦第六巡回上诉法院在《Hello Farms Marketing MI诉GR Vending MI》案中的判决，再次证明联邦大麻禁令可能具有法律意义。法院裁定，在联邦法院中，涉及大麻的合同因违反联邦法律而无效，并推翻了下级法院的相反判决。

法官纳尔班迪亚在法院判决书中总结了案情：密歇根州大麻种植商Hello Farms与被告GR Vending和CURA MI签订了供应大麻的合同。当GR Vending违约时，Hello Farms提起诉讼，陪审团判决Hello Farms赔偿3180万美元。被告辩称，由于合同在联邦法律下是非法的，下级法院在处理非法性抗辩时犯了错误。

当双方签订合同时，联邦法律将种植、分销和持有大麻定为犯罪。密歇根州，与许多其他州一样，将其视为合法商业。然而，尽管密歇根州合法化了大麻，联邦法院仍无法执行违反联邦法律的协议。我们推翻这一判决。

这个案例强化了我在相关研究（包括我的书《大麻联邦主义：山姆大叔与玛丽简》）中试图阐明的观点：如果我们想要真正的大麻联邦主义，让各州能够有效地尝试不同的大麻政策，仅仅依靠联邦政府的无为而治是不够的。联邦政府必须使州际实验合法化，例如通过结束对符合州法的行为的刑事化（同时继续禁止违反州法的行为，包括跨州贩运等）。这是联邦政府在禁酒令结束时对待酒精的方式，也是消除联邦禁令扭曲影响的唯一途径。
articles.summary:
Two-dozen states have legalized the adult possession of marijuana under state law. Many more have legalized the possession and use of marijuana for medicinal purposes. Yet marijuana distribution and possession remain illegal under federal law.

The federal government may not devote significant resources toward enforcing federal marijuana prohibition, but the fact that marijuana is illegal under federal law can still have meaningful consequences (though fewer for gun owners than before, thanks to the Supreme Court's decision in United States v. Hemani).

A case in point that federal marijuana prohibition can have legal significance is today's decision by the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit in Hello Farms Marketing MI v. GR Vending MI, holding that a marijuana contract is unenforceable in federal court given the illegal subject matter and throwing out a contrary district court ruling.

Judge Nalbandian summarizes the case in his opinion for the court:

Hello Farms, a Michigan marijuana grower, entered a contract to supply marijuana to Defendants GR Vending and CURA MI. When GR Vending breached, Hello Farms sued. And a jury awarded Hello Farms $31.8 million. Defendants argue that because the contract was illegal under federal law, the district court erred by not granting them judgment as a matter of law on their illegality defense.

When the parties contracted, federal law made the growth, distribution, and possession of marijuana a crime. Michigan, like many other states, made it a business. But despite the legalization of marijuana in Michigan, federal courts cannot enforce agreements to commit federal crimes. We reverse

This case underscores a point I have tried to make in my work on this subject (including in my book Marijuana Federalism: Uncle Sam and Mary Jane): If we want to have real marijuana federalism, in which states can experiment productively with different approaches to marijuana, it is not enough for the federal government to do nothing. It must make state experimentation legal, such as by ending the criminalization of conduct that is legal under applicable state law (while continuing to prohibit conduct that is illegal under applicable state law, including interstate trafficking in violation of the such laws). This was the federal government's approach to alcohol at the end of prohibition, and it is the only way to have a marijuana federalism that is free of the distorting effects of federal prohibition.

The post Marijuana Contracts Are Not Enforceable in Federal Court appeared first on Reason Magazine.

articles.title: Why Postliberalism Failed--And Is Likely to Fail Again
articles.content:
《基维塔斯展望》近期发表了一个小型研讨会，回应詹姆斯·帕特森和托马斯·豪斯的新书《为什么后自由主义失败》。参与者包括理查德·莱因施、大卫·谢弗以及本人。

我在研讨会中的贡献《后自由主义的前史》指出，对美国政治传统和保守主义的后自由主义批判并不新鲜，其理论基础也并非首次出现。正如帕特森和豪斯所言，这些背后的理念曾在其他国家被应用过，且效果恶劣。我补充道，这些观点在美国右翼中也曾有追随者，如今也不应具备比当时更大的说服力。

摘自我的文章：
保守派的立场很少因现代政治而产生满足感。现有秩序总是受到混乱和衰败的威胁。因此，一些人可能会发现后自由主义的批判观点颇具吸引力，甚至令人耳目一新。然而，除了当下政治背景外，针对古典自由主义、融合主义共识或美国建设的批判中，其实少有新意。无论其追随者是否意识到，后自由主义的指控不过是重温了多次被提出的论点，并提出了一个从未实现其捍卫者所声称的道德国家的治理模式。这条路已被反复踩踏，但收效甚微。

在《为什么后自由主义失败》一书中，詹姆斯·M·帕特森和托马斯·D·豪斯详细剖析并揭露了后自由主义项目，特别是它在天主教政治传统中的体现，包括天主教整体主义。结果是一个意识形态，它更关注的是“强大的中央政府从上而下对所有国民（无论其信仰如何）强加一种基于神学的公共利益愿景”，而非保护传统宗教社区。正如帕特森和豪斯所指出，这是“穿上天主教外衣的威权主义”。

最具价值的是，他们展示了后自由主义思想者所拥抱的理念并不新鲜，曾经被尝试过，且最终以失败告终。20世纪曾存在多个天主教导向的后自由主义政权，且均短暂、凶残。无论在葡萄牙、巴西、阿根廷、奥地利、斯洛伐克还是维希法国，天主教相关的后自由主义政权最终都以失败告终，常常留下压迫、苦难和死亡……

后自由主义对美国保守主义的指控——若非战术议程——回响了20世纪60年代末至70年代初保守运动内部的争论，主要（但不限于）在费城学会和《国家评论》的篇章中……

美国幸好未能孕育后自由主义的追随者。尽管有一些人试图将反动的欧洲保守主义引入美国，但他们未能动摇自二战以来定义美国保守运动的融合主义共识——这种共识致力于在限制和分权的政府框架内保护个人自由和传统道德……

我的文章结尾：
正如萨尔瓦多·约瑟夫·科尔代罗内大主教在《为什么后自由主义失败》的序言中所言，“对过去美好时代的幻想主义重申并非创造性的表现，而是历史健忘的迹象。”在这一点上，当代后自由主义或许是这个时代的合适意识形态——但这并不意味着其议程是好的，更不用说是美国的。

所有三篇贡献均可在此找到。

文章《为什么后自由主义失败——且很可能再次失败》最初发表于《理性杂志》。
articles.summary:
Today Civitas Outlook published a mini-symposium responding to the new book, Why Postliberalism Failed by James Patterson and Thomas Howes. Contributors include Richard Reinsch, David Schaefer. and yours truly.

My own contribution to the symposium, "The Pre-History of Postliberalism," explains how the postliberal critique of the American political tradition and American conservatism is not new, nor are the theoretical claims upon which it relies. As Patterson and Howes point out, the underlying ideas have been deployed before--and to quite ill effect--in other countries. As I add, these ideas have had adherents on the American right before, and they should be no more convincing today than they were then.

From my essay:

A conservative disposition is rarely conducive to contentment with contemporary politics. The existing order is always threatened by chaos and decay. So it is understandable why some may find the postliberal critique engaging, and perhaps even refreshingly transgressive. Yet aside from the political moment in which it is put forth, there is little in this critique of classical liberalism, the fusionist consensus, or the American project which is particularly new. Whether recognized by its adherents or not, the postliberal indictment rehashes arguments and propositions made many times before and proposes a model of governance that has never delivered the moral state its proponents claim it seeks. This ground is well-trod, but not to good effect.

In Why Postliberalism Failed, James M. Patterson and Thomas D. Howes usefully dissect and expose the postliberal project, particularly as it has manifested itself within the Catholic political tradition, including Catholic integralism. The result is an ideology less concerned with the preservation of traditional religious communities than with harnessing "a powerful, centralized government imposing from the top down a theologically-informed vision of the public good on all national subjects regardless of their faith." It is, Patterson and Howes note, "authoritarianism dressed up in Catholic vestments."

Perhaps most valuably, they show how the ideas embraced by postliberal thinkers are not new, have been tried before, and have ended in failure. There were multiple, Catholic-oriented postliberal regimes in the twentieth century, and all were nasty, brutish, and short. None yielded a sustainable or workable—let alone desirable—polity. Whether in Portugal, Brazil, Argentina, Austria, Slovakia, or Vichy France, Catholic-aligned postliberal regimes all ended in failure, often leaving oppression, misery, and death in their wakes. . . .

Much of the postliberal indictment of American conservatism—if not the tactical agenda—echoes arguments debated within the conservative movement in the late 1960s and early 1970s, largely (but not exclusively) at the Philadelphia Society and in the pages of National Review. . . .

America is fortunate that advocates of postliberalism failed to find a following here. While some sought to import a reactionary European conservatism to these shores, they failed to dislodge the fusionist consensus that has defined the American conservative movement since World War II—a consensus committed to individual liberty and traditional morality within a constitutional order that limits and decentralizes government power.  . . .

My essay concludes:

As Archbishop Salvatore Joseph Cordileone notes in his foreword to Why Postliberalism Fails, "A fantasized idealism of the past that would reassert such ideas is not a sign of originality, but of historical amnesia." In that regard, contemporary postliberalism is perhaps a fitting ideology for the age—but that hardly makes its agenda a good one, let alone an American one.

All three contributions may be found here.

The post Why Postliberalism Failed--And Is Likely to Fail Again appeared first on Reason Magazine.
